commentary: Henry starts off full on the stumps and Samson keeps it out. 132.7kph
pre_text:
Matt Henry has the new ball in hand. Henry has dismissed Samson twice in three T20I innings with the batter scoring just 15 runs.

6.58pm Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson complete their pre-game rituals and walk out after bumping fists. The New Zealand players take their positions. "India, India" chants are getting louder as the first ball approaches. Pitch has a covering of grass and there may be some swing movement early on but it's predicted to be a belter. Anti-dew spray was also used to try and negate the impact of dew.

Thanks, Shashank. I definitely can feel the excitement. The stadium is absolutely buzzing. All that remains is the action to begin.

Udana with the boldest prediction I've seen for any game: "65 will be scored off Bumrah today.!"

6.50pm  Rohit Sharma & MS Dhoni bring the trophy out to a massive roar from the crowd. The teams will soon join them in lining up for the anthems. I'd think there must be over a 100,000 people in already. Abhimanyu is back into the hot seat as 100 starry-eyed kids come out onto the field with the flags of India and New Zealand. Can you feel the excitement?

Jacob says: "Neesham lucky to get a game here. McConchie offers more with bat and ball. "


It's toss time! Ravi Shastri as usual with the honours. Tails is the call from Santner, tails it is.  New Zealand opt to bowl.  

"This is what we play the game for, gonna be a great night, hopefully we'll put up a good show," Santner says. Cole McConchie misses out tonight; Jacob Duffy comes in.

Suryakumar Yadav announces an unchanged India XI. That means Varun Chakravarthy keeps his place.

India: Samson, Abhishek, Ishan (wk), Surya (capt), Hardik, Tilak, Axar, Dube, Arshdeep, Varun, Bumrah

New Zealand: Allen, Seifert (wk), Rachin, Phillips, Chapman, Mitchell, Santner (capt), Neesham, Henry, Duffy, Ferguson



Nick says: "Tuning in from Christchurch, had a nap this afternoon and raring to go!"

Aarush Subraman: "Watching with my family from Atlanta, Georgia! We lost sleep because of daylight savings but the anticipation has overcome any tiredness we may be feeling."



Our readers from New Zealand: joining us from Auckland & Whagarei to Queenstown & Tauranga to Christchurch & Hamilton - how are you following this? What are you doing to stave off sleep? Or has that completely disappeared in anticipation of something special early on a Monday morning? Tell us, I'm all ears! Not long to go for the toss.




Why have New Zealand been so successful? A small teaser from Fidel:

"It's because their tournament outlook has been to adapt strategies and personnel specifically for the next challenge - the opposition they are facing and the grounds they are playing on." Dig in for the full piece here

6.10pm  Okay, now to Abhi's second question on 'win toss, and?'.....well, I'll let the master tactician Gaurav Sundararaman decode that for us.

Andrew Fernando from Ahmedabad: "Little less than half an hour before toss, and the pre-match entertainment is in full swing. This vast stadium is probably 40% full already, and the roads outside are packed. They make you trek at least a kilometre in from the ground, but it was pretty orderly and efficient when I came in. 

"Compared to the Gandhi Ashram where I'd just been, this is an entirely different vibe. Still a mild dominance of Virat shirts, but plenty of Hardik shirts, this being his home state. But not much for actual hometown boy Jasprit Bumrah."


6pm  Thanks, Abhi. Hello all. First things first. The atmosphere in Ahmedabad is electric, but what I'm most pleased is to see Bengaluru gear up for the final by staying indoors. 

Absolutely no traffic! A distance that takes me 90 minutes most days took me just about half the time. And those on the roads were all in blue jerseys. How's the atmosphere in your cities and how are you planning to watch the final? Let me know in the comments.




Time to say hi to Shashank for the first time today. Shanky, the toss is in around 30 minutes. What do you think the captain who wins that is going to do today? And do you think the team that wins the toss will hold a massive edge?

5.55pm He bowls in the powerplay and death, he finishes with the bat, and in the field India place him at hotspots during the high-pressure moments. Here is Karthik Krishnaswamy on India's big-match boss, Hardik Pandya.

Meanwhile, New Zealand also have an allrounder who lit up one World Cup with the bat, and is now doing so with the ball. Deiva Muthu wrote on Rachin Ravindra's second World Cup surge.

The pre-match show has begun with Falguni Pathak singing to a semi-full stadium that's getting more packed with each minute.

Elsewhere, another Indian is involved in a massive final, with Lakshya Sen aiming to become the first Indian since 2001 to win the prestigious All-England Badminton championships. Follow live coverage of his ongoing final, here.

Sudarshan KM : "My cousin has gone to Ahmedabad from Chennai along with his work friends. He has reached the stadium and just now said that the atmosphere is absolutely electric. A music "



5.45pm India won the 2024 T20 World Cup, but have gone on to stretch the limits of T20 batting since then, becoming a unit that now looks even more dangerous and difficult to beat. Behind this improvement has been a commitment to batting with no brakes on. Andrew Fidel Fernando looks at India's batting revolution ahead of the grand finale.

The orange seats are slowly turning blue as the home fans start to stream in. They will also be in for a show, with Falguni Pathak and Ricky Martin set to dazzle the crowds before the game. There is a blue stage set all around the centre pitch, where the performances will take place.

Mustafa Moudi: "Wishing a Very Happy Birthday to Ross Taylor, Jonty Rhodes, Charles Coventry and Harmanpreet Kaur. Hope this final makes their birthday memorable !!" -- I don't think Ross taylor and Harmanpreet Kaur can both be happy with the result of the final.

5.32pm The New Zealand bus has also arrived and the players are making their way into the stadium. 

MC: "Thought I'd give a shout to Alan Gardner's Star Wars-laden piece on how the dying art of off-spin could be the hero here. Made me chuckle + learned something" -- Thank you for saving me the trouble of figuring out how to plug this beauty.

5.30pm New Zealand captain Mitch Santner spoke before the game and said he won't mind if the New Zealand 'nice guys' turn heartbreakers today, to lift a trophy. His Indian counterpart, Suryakumar meanwhile has a simple message for his team: "be courageous".

Jaggu: "@Abhimanyu there is merit in what Sowmya is saying. While we can stick with Abhishek, surely they must have debated bringing in Kuldeep in place of Varun. He has been really struggling. And with no time for calming his nerves, Ind should bring in Kuldeep. " - That is a possibility explored by Karthik Krishnaswamy.

Srihari : "Fielding will be a key differentiator between the two teams today"

5.20pm One of the team buses is rolling in. There are plenty of cars already parked at the Motera. And it's the Indian team that's arrived first.

Sowmya : "@ Chuvi : what if those players in poor form fail to deliver tonight ? Just because we won the SF with a 11 , doesn't mean we have to stick to it. Merit " - Those players are in the team because of their ability. Take Abhishek for example. If you see what he has done in the two years leading up to this World Cup, which is a much larger sample size, it becomes hard to drop him mid-tournament.

pramod: "out of the box question- after tournament gets over what will happen to so many writers, sub editor, analysts, commentators and cricinfo network " -- We move on to the IPL, and once that's done the next series or tournament... not like there is ever a shortage of cricketing action!

Pratham : "On board a flight to NY over the Atlantic Ocean! No sights or sounds! Just you and me, ESPNCricinfo! Let's gooo!"

Shubha : "A fervently appeal to the ICC : should dew be a significant factor in the future, irrespective of the venue,start games at 8pm so that no team is at a distinct (dis) advantage after the toss. "

5.10pm We have plenty of reading material to warm you up for the final. Your starting point should of course be Sid Monga's preview. Team news, players to watch, stats and trivia and all the context you need -- he's got you covered.

Sunitha : "Life lessons same as sport. A month ago Abhishek Sharma was the hottest topic , he couldn't put a foot wrong. Cometh yhe WT20 everything has turned upside down for him. Something inside yours truly feels that Abhishek Sharma would deliver a strong performance tonight. " -- The good thing India have done is to stick with him. 

Chuvi : "Just don't tinker with your winning 11 - despite the poor form"

Sujatha : "The way Mitch Santner's overall game has reached reached another level is a lesson in itself for every captain. He has delivered the goods every since he was made captain. What an inspiration!"

Prem: "People might have queued up in front of Narendra Modi stadium as soon as the entry started...And I am queued up here on cricinfo to get my first comment published as soon as the coverage started." -- People have indeed started to take their seats.

5pm After 30 days and 54 games, we are finally ready for the grand finale of the 2026 T20 World Cup, and what a mouthwatering clash we have in front of us.

Defending champions India, backed by the richest board in cricket and stacked with so much talent that some players who'd waltz into most teams' playing XI don't even make their squad and no one bats an eyelid, have spent the last two years building a superteam that has pushed the barriers of T20 cricket. They have been here before - in fact at this very venue - in 2023, only to face heartbreak. But today, with the dreams of around 1.5 billion people pinned on them, they will be hoping to erase past scars and etch their names in history as the first team to win three men's T20 World Cup titles.

New Zealand, billed as the perennial underdogs, have limited resources - definitely so when compared to their opponents today - but arguably, no teams in the last decade or so have been as intelligent or effective in making the most of what they have, and have made it to their sixth major white-ball final in 11 years. In all five previous occasions, they fell at the final hurdle, but will hope that all their preparation and planning will get them over the line today to win their first men's World Cup title.

Destructive batters, wily and skillful bowlers, electrifying fielders - the two teams have all the ingredients needed to cook up a storm and leave a few jaws dropped on floors. Hello everyone, I'm Abhimanyu, and I'll be joined soon by Shashank Kishore as we bring to you ESPNcricinfo's live commentary for this World Cup final in Ahmedabad.

commentary: Raps him on the front pad! They have a discussion and choose not to review. This is on a length outside off and jags in. Possible inside edge? Yep, replay confirms it
Full outside off, hint of shape away, bunted to point
Full around off, Samson had taken a step back into his crease, and he works it to mid-on

Swung over mid-on and the crowd find their voice! This time he took a step forward before the ball was bowled. Henry bowls it on a length outside off and Samson just stands still and pumps it down the ground
Full around off, tapped towards mid-on and they sneak a quick single
ON a length outside off, Samson eases it down the ground to long-on
pre_text: No McConchie no offspin? Well not quite so. India have to face Glenn Phillips in the powerplay now! No team in this World Cup has fared poorer against offspin as India have!

short_text: Phillips to Abhishek Sharma, no run
commentary: Tossed up full outside off, Abhishek watchfully drives to cover

short_text: Phillips to Abhishek Sharma, no run
commentary: 92.6kph, full on middle, Abhishek blocks on the front foot
On a length outside off, Abhishek punches it down to long-off
Full-ish outside off, Samson works it down the ground to long-on
pre_text: This is the first time Phillips has ever bowled in the powerplay in T20Is!

commentary: Great fielding by Mitchell! Floated full outside off from wide of the crease, Abhishek drills a drive wide of long-off. Mitchell runs a long way and puts in the dive to save two runs
pre_text: Ravi: "Abhishek Sharma will click today"

commentary: Full on middle, 140kph, tucked in front of square leg
pre_text: Third over in the powerplay. Third different bowler. Here's Jacob Duffy

commentary: Abhishek dances down as Duffy tries to bowl it across him and away from his arc. Umpire signals for wide
Clears mid-on. This is pitched up on leg at 140kph and Abhishek heaves it down the ground. Doesn't get it off the middle but gets enough on it
Much more convincing, this shot! In the slot on middle and he lofts it straight of mid-off. One bounce four. He picked the slower ball well

Almost carries to deep square leg! Duffy goes short and Abhishek takes him on with the pull. doesn't time it but it's dying on Phillips who runs in from the rope and puts in the dive, but it still falls short of him
Samson looks to take on this length ball after going deep in his crease. Gets it off the bottom half of the bat to midwicket
Pumped over the bowler. Duffy overpitches outside off and Samson drives through the line. Duffy had no chance to stop that on the follow through and that goes for the third boundary of the over
Edge flies over the keeper! Back of length and angled across him at 143.2kph, Abhishek dances down and has a swupe and gets a thick edge that goes fine on the off side
pre_text: Fourth bowler for the fourth over. Lockie Ferguson

commentary: Slower ball dispatched! That was a slower ball angled across him, but it's overpitched and Abhishek picks it up early. Clears his front leg and launches hits over mid-off for an 85m six
Steers this length ball square on the off side for a single
142kph short ball angled across, Samson looks to help it along but can't connect as it goes down the line. Called wide
Leading edge flies for six! 145kph length ball on off angled across, Samson looks to whip it leg side but the leading edge off the toe of the bat sails behind point and goes all the way!
pre_text: Asiff: "Why have you brought Duffy when Henry was getting some swing in this batting paradise??"

commentary: A bit wayward and well down leg from Ferguson now
Another wide down the leg side
Looks for the wide slower yorker, Samson waits on it and squeezes it to point
Clipped fine of the short fine leg fielder! Big, big over this! 147kph length ball on the pads, Samson just helps it along and even the fielder's dive doesn't help
Goes for the wide yorker, but this goes past the wide line
pre_text: NZ bring back Matt Henry to try and stop the flow of runs

commentary: It's another wide yorker that has Richard Illingworth raising his arms
Length ball angled across him, Abhishek cuts it away through the gap to deep backward point
pre_text: Arav: "This feels like really poor captaincy. Why would you keep changing bowlers when one of them had clearly extracted something from the pitch?"

commentary: Samson goes deep in his crease and waits on this slower ball, but it goes down leg. Seventh wide of the innings!
Pulled away on the bounce to deep midwicket. 122kph back of length delivery, Samson stands tall and swats it away
Wide No. 8! Looks to again take it away from Abhishek's arc but can't keep it within the wide line
Boom! Boshed over long-off! Walks across to this full ball on off angled across, picks the slower ball very well and crunches it down the ground
Low full toss outside off, driven wide of mid-off for a quick single
Length ball outside off, it's an offcutter at 122kph, Samson waits on it and pulls it in the gap between deep square leg and deep midwicket and is able ot pick up two
Pulled high but he clears the boundary! India flying in the final! Bumped in short outside off, Samson goes on the back foot and nails the pull over square leg. 60 runs off the last three overs!

Fortune favouring the brave there! Abhishek backs away as Duffy tries to follow him with a full ball. Low full toss in the end and Abhishek tries to drive it on the off side and gets an edge past the stumps and the keeper. And too fine for short third too
Abhishek Sharma is livin' la vida loca! This is a low full toss outside off and Abhishek lofts it down the ground with a check-drive

High in the air, and it clears the fielder giving chase, and to add insult to injury, he manages to deflect it onto the boundary rope. Full outside off, he has a swipe across the line and skies it. Chapman gives chase and dives, but the ball lands beyond him. As he is on the ground and tries to pull the ball back, he somehow manages to help it onto the ropes instead!
Abhishek skies it again and this time Chapman doesn't make a dive as it lands just short of the boundary
Out of form? Well, Abhishek has just hit an 18-ball fifty in the World Cup final! Takes on a length ball and heaves it over midwicket. Lands just short of the boundary.

short_text: Duffy to Abhishek Sharma, no run
commentary: Length ball angled across, he takes a step across and leaves it in the end, but it's not called a wide. This is the highest powerplay of this World Cup! This is also the highest partnership between these two in T20Is!
Full outside off, driven to extra cover
pre_text: Mitch Santner takes the ball now

commentary: Tossed up wide, and it beats the bat as Samson looks to drive on the off side
Full and closer to off this time, punched to cover
On a length outside off from wide of the crease. Samson hangs back and cuts it hard past a diving point fielder for four
Clipped off the pads through midwicket for a single
On a length and bowled across him, Abhishek reaches out and punches it out to deep point
pre_text: More from Sampath: India's 92 for 0 is the joint-highest powerplay total at the men's T20 World Cup, alongside West Indies' 92 for 1 vs Afghanistan in 2024.

commentary: Has he nicked that? He has! Crowd goes silent as Ravindra strikes first ball! Tossed up slow and quite wide. If Abhishek leaves that alone, it would likely get called a wide. But he looks to take it on and slashes at it. Ends up with a thin nick that Seifert gobbles up. Abhishek departs, but you'd think he has done his job
pre_text:
More left-arm spin. Rac hin Ravindra

8.55pm Well, India know after the semi-finals that they can't sit easy, even with a score in the 250s. Finn Allen in his last game against India hit a 38-ball 80 chasing 272 and he is in devastating form. India will need their bowlers to come good. They still can't take this lightly. New Zealand will take inspiration from Jacob Bethell's heroics and hope to pull off a win for the ages. We are almost ready to go.

Meanwhile, here's a fun stat from Sampath: India - first team with successive 250-plus totals in men's T20Is. Across all men's T20s, only Sunrisers Hyderabad (vs RCB and DC in 2024) have done that before.

Tilak takes this at long-on, and India become the first to win the T20 World Cup back-to-back! The ghosts of Ahmedabad 2023 have been exorcised. Everyone on the bench huddle together around the ropes, the India flags come out and everyone's on their feet. 86,000 happy fans sing  Vande Mataram. Coming back to the ball, it was an innocuous delivery, short and right in the swingingg arc, Duffy backed away and flat-batted that to long-on where Tilak took it well, fully aware of where the ropes were behind him. He popped the ball back up just as he felt like he may tip over, and then regained his composure to complete the catch!  India become the first team to win the T20 World Cup at home, and the first to do it back-to-back.
